stem: Which finding is characteristic of the early hyperdynamic ('warm') phase of septic shock?

options.A: Warm extremities with peripheral vasodilation and reduced systemic vascular resistance.
options.B: Markedly increased systemic vascular resistance as the defining early hemodynamic pattern.
options.C: An absence of meaningful peripheral perfusion changes.
options.D: Cool mottled skin is required before septic shock can be present.

rationale: Septic shock is a distributive shock in which systemic vasodilation lowers systemic vascular resistance. Early hyperdynamic or 'warm' shock can present with warm extremities and bounding pulses. Later shock may become cool as compensatory vasoconstriction and organ dysfunction progress. Therefore A is correct.
educational_objective: Recognize the early warm/hyperdynamic perfusion pattern of septic shock.
source_locator: Septic Shock — pathophysiology and History/Physical, warm shock; Bacterial Sepsis — hemodynamic pattern with low SVR
source_claim_supported: Early septic shock may be hyperdynamic/warm with systemic vasodilation, low SVR, warm extremities and bounding pulses; cool shock can occur later.

correction_summary: Removed the unnecessary septic-versus-cardiogenic comparison, which introduced a second disease construct, and focused the item on the directly supported early warm septic-shock pattern. Reduced difficulty from hard to easy.
audit_findings: NCBI StatPearls directly supports A. The revised item avoids overgeneralizing all septic-shock presentations and specifies the early warm phase. Independent second pass passed.
